active_sessions_note: sessions on which the book actually executed. Counted from executions, never from non-zero returns: funding accrues while a position is held without any order being placed

convention.calendar: the broker's own day (UTC+3), whose midnight is 21:00 UTC -- the session close used throughout. EVERY day is a row, including weekends: the derivatives venue trades 24/7, so Saturday funding is a fact about Saturday. A day with no trade is a zero, never a missing row
convention.measured: counted on the derivatives leg alone, the 2026-08-26/27 round trip reads -4.50 USD where the pair makes it +0.18; the book's sign inverted, from -1.80 to +3.19
convention.out_of_scope: fee-calibration executions on other instruments are inside the return, not treated as a capital adjustment. They are real money lost on the account inside the book's window, and excluding them would FLATTER the curve by 3.5% of its result
convention.pnl: combined across both venues on a single calendar: derivatives realised (fills - fees + funding), plus broker deals, plus the profit of opposite ticket PAIRS locked that day
convention.superseded_chain: this book's chain was restarted at this convention. The previous chain -- one leg, and the wrong sign -- is kept verbatim under books/maker_01/superseded/, never rewritten and never presented
convention.superseded_snapshots: sessions published before this correction carry the previous convention and are left untouched -- a chained, timestamped record is not rewritten. They are why snapshots exist for dates before this book's inception
convention.why_locked_pairs: the broker account is in hedging mode: an opposing order opens a second ticket rather than closing the first. A matched buy+sell pair has a combined profit that does not depend on the market price -- it cancels between the legs -- so the pair is economically realised the moment the second ticket opens, even though the broker still shows it as floating
convention.window: performance is measured from the operator-declared start of the bot. Earlier executions were manual fee calibration: they moved money, so they are inside the opening capital, and they are inside no performance figure

flat_at_close.note: the curve is a mark-to-market NAV. It is built from realised profit and loss, which is only the same number where the book is flat -- so flatness is verified at every session close rather than assumed. A close that was not flat stops the publication instead of being quietly dropped: a missing session is selection, which is what the chain exists to prevent

fx.note: the broker leg is in a foreign currency. Each session's leg is converted once, at that session's close rate, and never revalued -- so no exchange-rate movement enters the curve. A live dashboard that revalues the whole leg at the current rate will differ by a few cents; each snapshot publishes that gap as fx.delta_bps

inception_note: anchored to the equity held the session before the first execution, so that session's profit and loss sits inside the curve rather than behind its starting point
initial_capital_note: the book's size at the inception close, once the capital was fully paid in. It is the denominator of the percentage axis on the cumulative curve
opening_capital_note: the equity at the OPEN of the inception session -- a different number, because the deposit that funds the broker leg lands intraday. It is the denominator of the first day's return, and it is never published as a curve point: nothing before inception is

out_of_scope_total.note: fee-calibration executions on other instruments, excluded from the return and treated as a capital adjustment; the instruments are not published

reconciliation.note: the curve is reconstructed from realised profit and loss, so it is checked against what the two accounts actually report. The unrealised legs are added back before comparing, because while a position is open a realised series cannot equal a marked one — and in hedging mode that gap is structural: the closed leg realises while the opposite leg is still open. What is left is read drift: the two venues are queried one after the other while the account keeps trading. Published whether or not it is zero — a field that only appears when it is inconvenient is not a measurement

round_trips.combined_note: each round trip is the SUM of both legs. The broker account is in hedging mode, so its half only appears when a ticket is settled -- or never, while the ticket stays locked against an opposite one. Counted on the derivatives leg alone, the 2026-08-26/27 round trip reads -4.50 where it is +0.20
round_trips.unit_note: the unit of account is the round trip, not the session: this book executed on 3 of its 17 published sessions, so a session-based denominator would measure the calendar rather than the strategy
